chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to him via an ascending chain, from Hanzalah, from Maisar, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:
Two of you will not be seen in Hell, by Allah, nor even one.
I said: Where is that from the Book of Allah?
He kept silent from me for a year.
I was with him one day during circumambulation when he said to me: O Maisar, today I am permitted to answer your question thus.
I said: And where is it in the Quran?
He said: In the Surah 'Ar-Rahman', and it is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: (So on that Day none will be asked about his sin - among you - of man or jinn).
I said to him: It does not contain 'among you'!

He said: The first one who altered it was Ibn Arwa, because it was evidence against him and his companions, and if 'among you' were not in it, the punishment of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, would fall away from His creation.
If no man or jinn is asked about his sin, then for whom will Allah punish on the Day of Resurrection?

key_terms.ابْنُ أَرْوَى: Ibn Arwa (a known reciter/Qari who altered Quranic readings)

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam justify that believers will not be in Hell using Quran 55:39?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the exclusion of believers from Hell is rooted in Quran 55:39, arguing that the phrase 'among you' (min-kum) was originally present but altered by Ibn Arwa to preserve the logic of divine justice. This textual nuance ensures that while believers are exempt from questioning regarding their sins, punishment remains valid for others, thereby reconciling divine mercy with the necessity of retribution.
